new_findings.text: Heavy-stance Defence x0.8 has a THIRD confirmation nobody has banked, and it is entirely web-side — no android string and no wiki. The web v0.717 character sheet sets its defence modifier per stance at §1t5957s0§.as:2728 (light = 1), :2737 (balanced = 1) and :2746 (heavy = 0.8), and consumes it at :2947 as `int(_loc3_ * _loc47_)` beside the stance name — the positional twin of android InventoryUI.as:2166 `"physical def: " + int(defense * defModifier) + " (" + stanceName + ")"`. So in v0.717 the character sheet and the simulation AGREE on defence (§1t99s0§.as:3288 `return defense * 0.8;`), unlike the android build where they contradict each other on crit. That agreement is itself worth banking: it means the v0.717 char-sheet path is a usable cross-check, whereas the v0.682 one is not.

new_findings.text: UNCLAIMED AND LANE-RELEVANT: the web v0.717 character sheet carries a per-stance SLASH-DISTANCE ladder that no claim in this packet touches, and it is the mirror image of the damage ladder. In the same three stance branches that set damage and crit, §1t5957s0§.as sets a fourth modifier: :2729 light = 1.4 flat; :2738 balanced = 1 + 0.2*balancedMastery*0.1; :2747 heavy = 0.5 + 0.4*heavyMastery*0.1. It is consumed at :3013 as `int(_loc21_ * _loc48_)` beside the stance name — positionally the twin of android InventoryUI.as:2232 `"slash distance: " + int(baseSlashLength * slashModifier) + " (" + stanceName + ")"`, where the variable is literally named slashModifier. At mastery 10 the ladder reads Light 1.4 / Balanced 1.2 / Heavy 0.9, exactly inverting the damage ladder 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 that NEW-2 confirms from the same file. PARTIAL, not HELD, for one reason: this is the DISPLAY path, and NF-3/NF-5 prove a shipped build can display a modifier its own sim does not apply (v0.682 crit). It is not yet shown that the v0.717 sim uses the same coefficients — that needs the InputManager.setMaxDistance call site in the web bundle. What it does do is give the reach question its first ratio-shaped web-build evidence, and it is not a static text field, so SOURCE_CONSTANTS.md:33-36's placeholder ruling does not apply to it.
